Summary: The Senior Director, Clinical Science provides senior scientific and strategic leadership for the design, execution, and interpretation of clinical trials across one or more therapeutic programs. Experience in autoimmune, immunology, or inflammation indications strongly preferred.

Requirements:
Getting matched for an anesthesiologist job requires you to have a Bachelor's degree, four years of medical school, and 3-8 years in a residency program. Additionally, the United States Medical Licensing Examination is required, along with other licensure depending on the state. When it comes to filling open anesthesiologist positions, employers are looking for candidates who have dexterity, patience, leadership, and communication skills. It's also a plus to have experience in the fields of 
Surgery
, 
Internal Medicine
 or 
Family Medicine.
Anesthesiology Job Locations
Getting matched for an anesthesiology job typically means you'll be working in a hospital or outpatient clinic. Although, some positions are with research institutions where physicians study ways to improve the care for anesthesia patients and manage their pain.
Average Salary for Anesthesiologist Jobs

A physician in anesthesiology can typically expect to make between $321,000 and $420,000. The current median annual salary is $370,712 as of early 2018. These salaries can vary considerably based on geographic location of practice, years of experience and the levels of care provided.

Whether you are a young professional looking to gain experience or an established physician looking for a change, our advanced search tool can help find an anesthesiologist job right for you.
With only a few clicks, you'll find hundreds of active anesthesiology opportunities in a variety of settings listed directly by employers looking for medical professionals just like you!

The Mailroom COE Associate oversees and coordinates the work of all mailroom vendor partners supporting Cognizant's clients, ensuring operational accuracy, timeliness, compliance, and service-level performance. This role is the primary operational liaison between internal teams, client stakeholders, and vendor partners - driving daily production oversight, issue resolution, performance monitoring, reporting, and new client implementation support across mailroom intake, sorting, scanning, indexing, fulfillment, and correspondence handling.

In this role, you will:

-Monitor daily vendor operations (intake, sorting, scanning, indexing, fulfillment, exception handling) and track performance against SLAs, turnaround times, and quality standards.

-Lead vendor governance meetings, including metrics, issue logs, and root cause analysis.

-Support onboarding of new clients, workflows, and mailroom requirements as the mailroom SME.

-Define scope, volumes, SLAs, and reporting needs with cross-functional teams.

-Document SOPs and process flows; support testing, pilots, training, and cutover.

-Monitor early-life production and drive issue resolution post-go-live.

-Serve as liaison across client, operations, and vendor teams on inventory status, priorities, and exceptions.

-Escalate risks, delays, and compliance concerns promptly.

-Support capacity, holiday, and business continuity planning with the COE lead.

-Monitor HIPAA/PHI, data privacy, and chain-of-custody adherence.

-Support corrective action plans for defects, missed SLAs, or misrouted/delayed documents.

-Participate in audits and control reviews; keep documentation current.

-Prepare daily/weekly/monthly performance reports; analyze volume, aging, and defect trends.

-Recommend processes, automation, and reporting improvements to leadership.

About the job:
Title:
 Director of Quality

Location:
 United States-Alabama-Fort Rucker

Job Number:
 18704

This position is pending contract award. If AAR is awarded this contract, the estimated start date is October 1, 2026.

Description

The Director of Quality is responsible for establishing, executing, and maintaining a comprehensive Quality Control (QC) and Quality Management System (QMS) that ensures all aircraft, training devices, maintenance activities, and supplier provided products meet AAR, OEM, FAA, and Government customer requirements. This role oversees all aspects of the Aircraft Maintenance Program's Environment, Health, and Safety program and serves as the functional supervisor for all Quality Control Inspectors assigned to the CBP Program.

The Director of Quality acts as the primary liaison with Government oversight representatives, the Helicopter OEM, and the FAA, ensuring full compliance with contractual, regulatory, and training related quality requirements. This position is accountable for audit readiness, Government surveillance support, and timely response to all findings, observations, and Corrective Action Requests (CARs).

What You Will Be Responsible For

Develop, implement, and maintain the Quality Control Plan (QCP) and Quality Management Plan (QMP) across all assigned locations in coordination with Senior Leadership.

Lead and manage a comprehensive flight training Quality Control program, ensuring all aircraft, training operations, and maintenance activities meet mission, safety, and regulatory requirements.

Ensure all aircraft are safe, mission-ready, properly configured, and delivered on schedule in accordance with daily flight training and operational requirements.

Support daily maintenance operations to ensure all contractual requirements, performance standards, and mission objectives are met or exceeded.

Support Government surveillance IAW the Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan (QASP), ensuring continuous compliance and readiness for all Government evaluations.

Ensure audit readiness by maintaining complete, accurate, and accessible records, documentation, and quality artifacts.

Provide Government representatives access to records, facilities, personnel, and quality documentation as required for surveillance, audits, and inspections.

Respond to Government findings, observations, and CARs within Government-directed timelines, ensuring timely corrective and preventive action implementation.

Identify operational risks and support development of mitigation strategies to ensure mission continuity and contract success.

Prepare and present program status updates, performance metrics, and operational reports to Senior Leadership.

Foster effective communication and collaboration across all program functions.

Promote a culture of safety, quality, accountability, and continuous improvement.

Perform all other duties as assigned.
